newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Kohl's Manila visit to reap $1-bln business deals.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's Manila visit to reap $1-bln business deals.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl began a three-day visit to the Philippines on Tuesday that is expected to be crowned by almost $1 billion in business deals.
The first German head of government to visit the Philippines arrived from Indonesia and headed straight to a park where he laid flowers at a monument to Filipino hero Jose Rizal.
From the park, he proceeded to the Malacanang presidential palace for one-on-one talks with President Fidel Ramos.

After their talks, the two leaders were to witness the signing by German and Filipino businessmen of agreements on energy, telecommunications and port construction worth $949 million. Kohl is accompanied by a 130-member delegation that includes 30 top German businessmen.
"This visit brings economic cooperation between the two countries to a new plateau," European Chamber of Commerce vice president Henry Schumacher told Reuters.
He said that besides the signing of the business deals at the palace, Kohl's visit was also expected to hasten agreement on the setting up of a "German Centre" in Manila.
The centre will serve as a liaison point for German businessmen in the Philippines.
"We want the Germans to strengthen their economic presence in the country," Philippine Foreign Office assistant secretary Luz Palacios said. "That will be our main pitch."
Palacios said she did not expect any major political bilateral issue to crop up in Kohl's talks in Manila. "Relations between out two countries are very smooth," she said.
One accord to be signed during Kohl's visit is an agreement between the two governments to promote and protect investments.
The business deals to be signed on Tuesday would significantly boost German investments in the Philippines which amounted to only $71.5 million over a 10-year period from 1986 to 1995.

The deals include an agreement by Siemens AG with the Philippines' First Gas Holdings Corp to build a gas-fired, 990-megawatt power plant in Batangas province just south of Manila. The project is worth $650 million.
First Gas is a joint venture of British Gas and First Philippine Holdings Corp.
Executives of Deutsche Telekom and Asiacom cellular phone subisidiary IslaCom were also to sign a $266 million joint venture agreement, officials said.
Details of the joint venture were not available but IslaCom president Cesar Campos previously told reporters Telekom would take a 35 percent stake in its parent.
A third deal to be signed on Tuesday is a $33 million financial cooperation agrement for port construction and navigational aids for Philippine inter-island shipping.

The Philippines has a reputation as a country prone to maritime disasters. More than 3,000 people were killed when an inter-island ferry and a tanker collided in 1988 in the central Philippines in the world's worst peace time sea disaster.
Despite its relatively small investments so far, Germany ranks as the Philippines' eighth largest trading partner with total trade between them amounting to close to $2 billion.
The Philippines is the second leg of Kohl's Asian tour which will also take him to Japan.

His visit to Manila coincided with calls from Germany's opposition Social Democrats for the Chancellor to break off his Asian trip to answer questions in parliament about the German budget. Kohl's office said he would not do so.
